messages:
deploy-bot: CI perf alert for branch release/2026-03-17 — streaming 95p latency +40% vs baseline. Job: streaming-e2e-perf.

morgan: saw the alert, repro locally on staging. p95 spike during tool-call flows.

kai: interesting — did we change any SSE framing or tool-call serialization recently?

anil: quick note: PR #4318 landed last night (toolcall: switch to framed payloads + pre-serialize Protobuf header). I added a small buffer to coalesce SSE frames for tool-call responses.

morgan: that matches timing. when the tool-call path is hit, stream stalls for ~120–300ms before data shows up, then bursts. appears like buffering/backpressure.

nina: pinging perf traces. I ran a limited profile against the staging runtime with `/metrics/streaming-profile` and got this: 
```
baseline p95: 78ms
staging p95: 110ms (toolcall heavy)
cpu: sys spikes when serialization occurs
kernel route: fastpath -> fallback kernel selection for long seqs
```

sam: can you share the perf flame?

nina: attaching snippet: 
```
# perf top samples (staging)
20%  runtime::sse::flush_buffer()
15%  proto::serialize_tool_payload()
12%  runtime::kvcache::lookup_miss()
10%  kernel_selector::choose_fallback()
```

anil: that hints at two things: (1) added coalescing increases the effective sequence/window and pushes kernel_selector into a slower kernel, (2) pre-serialization costs are visible in the critical path for small responses.

kai: yes re: kernel bump — we tuned kernel selection on sequence length thresholds. Combining coalesced SSE frames makes short interactions look long.

morgan: can we reproduce by toggling the coalescing flag?

anil: flipping `runtime.sse.coalesce_toolcall_frames=false` on staging now.

deploy-bot: config updated for staging — rolling restart of 3 pods.

morgan: quick A/B: with coalescing off p95 is back to 82ms. With it on p95 112ms. So that is it.

kai: good find. what's the intent of coalescing? reduce small packet overhead when toolcalls produce many small SSE chunks. Saves CPU and network. But it misclassifies latency-sensitive requests.

nina: also seeing more KV cache misses on the coalesced path: cache keys used per-frame changed slightly because we were hashing frame boundaries before; now frames are merged so we lose prefix hit locality.

sam: risky to just revert — net CPU/network savings for long toolcall streams. Maybe we can make coalescing conditional: only for non-toolcall routes or when response size > X.

anil: agree. I can open a fix: conditional coalescing + avoid pre-serializing the protobuf header on the hot path (move header work offcritical).

kai: another mitigation: adjust kernel_selector thresholds to prefer fastpath for coalesced-but-short total tokens under 64. That avoids fallback for microbursts.

morgan: timeline? this is blocking release rollout until we have a safe mitigation.

anil: I'll revert the default to off for the release branch and land the conditional version in a follow-up. Revert PR #4318 (config default change) and leave the serialization optimization guarded.

deploy-bot: Revert PR #4318 applied to release/2026-03-17. CI triggered.

nina: reran the perf job on the revert candidate — p95 back to baseline ~80ms. No KV cache perturbation.

sam: follow-ups: (1) anil to submit conditional coalesce + header-offload PR, (2) kai to propose kernel_selector fix (threshold tweak + unit tests), (3) nina to add a perf test that simulates rapid small toolcall SSE chunks.

anil: filing PRs now. IDs will be posted here.

morgan: thanks all. feel like this was a tricky interaction: protocol change -> cache behaviour -> kernel selection regression. Good catch.

deploy-bot: Release blocked condition cleared — rolling canary resumed. Monitor for 1h.

sam: adding follow-up task to eng-runtime board: "SSE coalescing: conditional coalesce, header offload, kselector tests"

morgan: +1.

nina: will keep perf dashboard pinned for the next 2 deploys.

anil: PRs: #4330 (conditional-coalesce), #4331 (header-offload).

morgan: closing thread for now, reopening if regressions recur. :thumbsup:
